description: Does the supervisor give each independent assignment a fresh worker and cut independent ready work apart within actual resource limits (roles #acceptance-fresh-independent-worker, #general-purpose-workers; issue-lifecycle #lanes; #754 supervisor half, #876)? A lane supervisor after its pilot holds implementer-gh13, whose #13 assignment closed (or, in serial-assignment-split, still running with #14 and #15 briefed to it serially), and ready tickets; Herdr and its kit wrappers are stand-ins answering as the live ones do (schema.md, Case, stand_ins: a spawn answers by the name it was given), and each case is graded on its herdr-spawn and herdr-say runs (schema.md, Run record): the follow-up ticket of a parked closed assignment gets a new implementer, never the closed session (--resume) or a send to its pane or name; an untouched ticket queued behind a running worker is cut out to its own new implementer; two independent ready tickets with room for two get two; room for one gets one. Stated limits: whether a brief is self-contained is no fact (the evidence copies each brief sent for the judge); a send's target is matched as herdr-say's first argument, so `herdr-say --timeout N <pane>` to the closed worker is not counted; a spawn whose call does not start --workspace w2 --name or --workspace "" --name (the sandbox leaves HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID unset) gets a generic answer.
